sn45.8:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach and analyze for you the noble eightfold path.
sn45.8:1.3: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”
sn45.8:2.1: “And what is the noble eightfold path?
sn45.8:2.2: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.
sn45.8:3.2: Knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.
sn45.8:4.2: It is the purpose of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.
sn45.8:5.2: Refraining from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
sn45.8:6.2: Refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and unchastity.
sn45.8:7.2: It’s when a noble disciple gives up wrong livelihood and earns a living by right livelihood.
sn45.8:8.2: It’s when a bhikkhu generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.
sn45.8:8.3: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.
sn45.8:8.4: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have not arisen do arise.
sn45.8:8.5: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fulfilled by development.
sn45.8:9.2: It’s when a bhikkhu meditates by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn45.8:9.3: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn45.8:9.4: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn45.8:9.5: They meditate observing an aspect of principles—ardently aware and comprehending, without craving and aversion towards the world
sn45.8:10.2: It’s when a bhikkhu, fully withdrawn from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and dwells in the first stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of seclusion, with thinking and considering.
sn45.8:10.3: As thinking and considering are stilled, they enter and dwell in the second stage of meditation, which has the delight and contentment born of concentration, with internal clarity and poise, without thinking and considering.
sn45.8:10.4: And with the fading away of delight, they enter and dwell in the third stage of meditation, where they meditate with equanimity, with awareness and comprehension, personally experiencing the contentment of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and aware, one meditates content.’
sn45.8:10.5: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and dwell in the fourth stage of meditation, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and awareness.
